terra.problem: The claim that people do not contend for something that changes shape is not necessarily true.
“Not even close” is a negative, discouraging response to the baker's answer.
Saying the cities show where the men's path ends extends Jude's comparison beyond what he states.
Jude says the things they do instinctively will destroy them, not that their instincts themselves will do it.
“No second chance” adds a conclusion that Jude does not state in the tree image.
The joke about a reserved seat makes light of the judgment described as blackest darkness forever.
Jude does not say the wandering stars have no spot in the sky.
A star without light is not necessarily a rock rolling around. The explanation presents an inaccurate claim as fact.
“Myriads” does not establish that the crowd is bigger than anyone could count.
Jude tells them to have mercy on those who doubt. He does not specify moving toward them or staying physically close.

“Unblemished and joyful” assigns the joy to those presented, while the verse does not specify whose joy it is. Calling the statement a promise also goes beyond Jude's statement that God is able to do this.
The joke about how big the sentence is makes the way Scripture is written the subject of the joke.
